I'm also wondering if anyone can relate to my experience.

Ever since I was a child and up to my sophmore year in high school I had always been awkward and nearly friendless. I had a few people I talked to but no one that I "hung out" with regularly and no one even close to a best friend.

About 2 years ago I started watching space documentaries and browsing the subreddit /r/space I watched Nearly all of Richard Dawkins, Lawrence Krauss, and Sam Harris's lectures and interviews on youtube. Lawrence Krauss's lecture on a Universe from Nothing and his book with the same title left my utterly amazed. Obviously it's not even close to being proven yet but the fact that respected physicists think our universe may have come from "Nothing" is amazing (It's not actually nothing. Go watch the doc).

Anxiety was a huge problem for me. I saw someone I knew. Do I look at them? Do I say Hi? Where do I put my hands? I just mumbled and they didn't hear me... fuck.

Well it's rather amazing but this Cosmic Perspective I've experienced has changed me.

I have an idea of how big the universe really is. After Playing Space Engine (A free game) I discovered just how big the universe really is. How big is the universe? We don't know. It could be infinite.

Either way just Flying through space engine literally brought tears to my eyes hours on end. That's when I knew I wanted to do something better with my life. I don't want to be socially awkward and die alone. I want to have friends and be happy.

In a way I now think I can do both better than the average person. Petty arguments over things that don't matter are a thing of the past for me.

My fear of talking to girls is gone. this is literally my mindset before I go talk to a girl that i'm interested in my class: "Well shit i'm nervous. What if this what if that.." turns into "The universe is fucking huge, you're going to die, and nobody cares." I then take a deep breath and do it.

This is not something I did overnight. It took many months of practice and I can say that a year ago today I was a very different person.

Sorry if this is out of order, grammatically incorrect, or lacks proper flow, I was on my phone.

I'm a lot happier now and just wanted to see if there are others like me who have had a similar experience. Thanks for redaing if you got this far.
